body.p: I'll tell a tale. The title is Dyooa. Dyooa has Bunelya. At some point, Dyooa went along his river. He was carried along the river by the stream[ShA:] The speaker was not sure in the meaning of kolarezʔ.. Then, his little river became big water. Where the river has become the big water, he saw a lean-to. He saw a lean-to. This lean-to shines at the sun. This lean-to was metallic, all made of copper metal. A boat is tied with an iron rope. A man sits on top. Dyooa, going along this river, slipped near the lean-to or he was brought by the stream of the river. Dyooa moored, looks up. The man from above says: "Dyooa, Dyooa, if you have come for a visit, I will tie your boat." Dyooa now sees, the one who spoke from above lowered a ladder from the lean-to. Well, let it be. Dyooa said: "I went up the iron ladder, I went up, and he is sitting. He said, he is making something. Near him, he said, there will be his huge, iron bow, his bow shines at the sun." Dyooa, as he sees, says: "It seems, he makes arrows, he adzes sticks for arrows. These wastes, these cuttings, Dyooa sees, they, - he says, - fly up as little birds. They fly away, - he says, - they fly away from here." Dyooa said: "Of course, I will eat, I would like to eat," - he said. Dyooa only looks. "Now, - he said, - we are not in a tent, after all. So what are we going to eat?" "Well, eat." Inak, he said, when he was sitting, had a rope. He moved his rope. "Nibiyu, Nibiyu, - he said, - a guest has come, send him something. It would be good to feed the guest." After a while, he pulled the rope so, he said, a cauldron was tied to the end of the rope, some dishes. "This, - he said, - the meat is totally hot, even steam comes from it after it is taken out of the water." Dyooa looks with his eyes wide-eyed. "This, - he said, - is what kind of person I have found." Dyooa ate, of course. After he ate, Dyooa said to Inak: "So, you, - he said, - come to visit me.". Inak said: "I don't have time, - he said, - but well, I'll come. Okay, I'll come, - he says, - when a few days will pass." "Come, come," - the other one said. Dyooa went down the ladder to his boat. Well, Inak, of course, gave some fish, he gave fish. Dyooa's boat is full of fish. Dyooa said to Nibiyu: "Today I met Inak, I visited Inak. Tomorrow, in two days, Inak will come to visit us. We as well, - he said, - something for Inak ... Of course, we will treat Inak, he seems to be saying. We have to prepare a treat for Inak. I, - he said, - during two days, - he said, - I have to make a lean-to". He said, I forgot this river.[ShA:] The general sense is/was unclear both to me and to my consultant. Inak ... Dyooa said then. Dyooa then, without thinking long, woke up the next day ... From the forest, the bank of the river was wooded, of course, Dyooa brought trees. Dyooa now ... made his lean-to on one leg. He made a ladder like Inak. After a while Dyooa finished making his lean-to. Then he said to, well, to Nibiyu: "Nibiyu, then, - he said, - Inak will come for a visit, I, - he said, - I will send you into the water. Prepare food. As soon as, - he said, - these ropes of mine will start moving, send it, up." What about Nibiyu? Of course, she boiled a cauldron, probably, they had something, food. So Nibiyu, well, she began to cook food. Well, after a while, Inak appeared along the river. His copper boat shines at the sun. Passing Dyooa's lean-to here on the boat ... If Inak waves his oar, Dyooa's lean-to trembles. Inak, sitting, said: "Dyooa's lean-to is trembling." Well, let it be. Dyooa speaks from above to Inak. "Inak, Inak, - he said, - tie your boat by the leg of the lean-to." He also had a ladder. Yes. Inak carefully tied his boat, it was with a rope. Well. While Inak was walking, Dyooa, of course, he probably had some kind of rope, probably he had something. And Dyooa put Nibiyu in a sack, then he stuffed some fish there, probably, stuffed some dishes, probably. He said: "Nibiyu, when my rope starts to move later, - he said, - these dishes, sent me dishes, - he says, - up with a rope.". And at this time, Nibiyu was alive. (...). Dyooa, while this one, well, while Inak was walking, drowned his friend, Nibiyu. After all, she has not drowned immediately, he used a stone to drown Nibiyu, so that she would go into the water. Well, after some time, Inak tied his boat to Dyooa's lean-to, he climbed up along Dyooa's ladder. The Dyooa's lean-to almost fell on its side, after Inak tied it. And Inak, it is heard, saying: "Dyooa's lean-to is trembling." Well, anyway, Inak got to this thing, well, got to Dyooa, and sat down carefully. Well. Dyooa, similar to Inak, is whittling some stick. From adzed sticks he makes arrows. He stacks his shavings nearby. Earlier, when he went to that one, well, to Inak, Inak's shavings flew up like birds, as one could see. And his shavings are lying quietly next to him, lying in a pile. Well, let them lie, well. Well, at some point he said to Inak: "Well, let me treat you," - he said. Now Dyooa began to move his rope, that was sent into the water. He drowned her, Nibiyu, with a stone. Dyooa, it is heard, saying: "Damn, she fell asleep, after all, - he said, - why she doesn't want to send us food, she fell asleep, after all", - he said. After a while, he pulled out the rope. At the end of this rope, Dyooa had tied dishes, dishes that people use for eating. Yes, then he pulled Nibiyu out: "Damn, - he said, - she is sleeping." When Dyooa saw Nibiyu: Nibiyu's eyes were like an ice of a lake. She choked on water, this one. What will happen then? Well, Inak said: "Well, I shouldn't eat, I'd better go home. He sees, things are bad, it seems. It seems, he has sent a person into the water, and it seems, she has drunk the water there, it seems, she has died there. She choked on the water," - Inak said. "Dyooa, some other time, I'll come, - he said, - it seems like it would be good for me to go home". "Damn, - he said, - she fell asleep, after all." Inak, well, went down, Dyooa's lean -to is trembling, he almost fell down. Inak sent his copper boat, on which he had arrived, back along the river. Dyooa said: "What should I do with this one, why did she die like that", - he said. After that, Dyooa put this Nibiyu in a boat and took her to his little grass tent. He put her in a boat, of course, he brought Nibiyu to the tent. Dyooa said: "What shall I do with this one now?" Now, well, Dyooa pulled out his knife, butchered the whole Nibiyu, took out whatever was from Nibiyu, hung it on a hanger, dried the meat of Nibiyu in the sun. Well, the sun, maybe there was the sun, maybe it dried up from the fire. He dries it like a dried fish. Well, and then ... And Dyooa is upstairs, Dyooa never stays at home. Dyooa walks above along the Earth, he found people there. He met people, Enets people with reindeer, they were dressed, he met people riding along the tundra. The also treated Dyooa there, of course, they fed him. Dyooa after a while said to these people. "You also come to visit me, - he said, - I'm a settled person, as for treating you, of course, I'll treat you, - he said, - I'll feed you. These friends of his said: "As for coming, that is, of course, we will come, - they said, - we will come, where is your tent?". Dyooa said: "If you walk along the river, - he said, - you will come, you will find my little tent, - he said, - is a little tent made out of grass.". Well. After a while, these people said. "Who was the person we have meet before? He said, - when people call me, - I am Dyooa." "Let's go to visit Dyooa." This man, of course, went, these people are Enets, good people, people living on Enets land. And he fished or did something else, he lived on a bank of his river. His wife's meat, well, he dried it well in the sun, or it dried up from the fire. After a while, the guests arrived. (...). "Dyooa, Dyooa, do you live alone?" - the friends asked. "Yes, - he said, - I live alone, I fish on this river, all my life, he said, I live here, only with fish, he said, I live, I only catch fish.". Dyooa said: "Now, - he said, - I should cook a cauldron for you. This is, - he said, - dried fish, - he said, - do you eat fish dried in the sun? Dyooa the meat of this old woman, dried by him, enough to eat ...[ShA:] The two sentences appear in the published version, but are absent in the audiorecording. Dyooa said after a while here. "How can I be now? That Bunelya of his is somewhere here, as well. Dyooa walked and walked around. When he walked around, well, there weren't many people there. Dyooa at some point then ... He drowned the wife of his in the water. Dyooa again brought his wife back from somewhere. And that Bunelya has already become big. A big guy. Bunelya has a bow, he made a bow. And Dyooa, well, he fishes in the river, he gets fish. Dyooa after a while says to that new Nibiyu. "Nibiyu, Nibiyu, it is probably my time to die now. I'll die now." Well, dead people knew, of course, that a person can die. Dyooa fell ill after a while. He fell ill, Dyooa did not live for a long time. Dyooa died. Well, his, well, his new, well, Nibiyu was left, his wife. His new wife said to Bunelya. "After that, we need to do something with our Dyooa. We will not leave him in plain sight. Somehow, - she said, - we have to do it. Well, how will we do it?" But what does Bunelya know? And the other, this Nibiyu, was already an old person. "Well, - he said, - we'll do it, let's make him a tent," - he said. And the house like a tent, this house like a tent, in our tradition they made a tomb tent for him. So, this is what Bunelya with Nibiyu did. How can it be good? There are gaps between the boards. Before that, Dyooa said when he was alive. Now, he said, we ... How it is now, you will not say. There was a cauldron or some kind of bowl. They made a wooden artifact, with birch bark. It is full. This fish caviar, he said. Well, when he was alive. As for caviar, - he said, - put it into my coffin. Then they, as Dyooa said earlier, did not even keep it for themselves to eat. They put this fish caviar into Dyooa's coffin. The two of them stayed. This guy is all over the place. Chasing some birds, he passed near the Dyooa's tomb tent. And there Dyooa says so. The guy sees him from time to time. Dyooa sits down from time to time. He says to this Bunelya: "Bunelya, ha-ha! Yes, when he opens his mouth, his mouth is full of fish caviar. Well. After a while, Bunelya then said to Nibiyu. "Nibiyu, Nibiyu, - he said, - when I pass by Dyooa's tomb tent there, Dyooa says to me: Bunelya, ha-ha!" And the old woman said. "Oh, what are you looking for in the land of the deceased, near a dead person? He starts showing up for you. Well." When he seems. Probably, Bunelya went not once, not twice. While walking around there. Bunelya said: "Some day I will deal with you. Just wait. Dyooa, probably you're not dead. Probably you're alive. Here." Then after a while Bunelya so. This river must have been already large enough to fish. "Oh," - Bunelya said. "The opposite side of our river, from the opposite side, he said, a polar bear has come, a polar bear. The polar bear came. And it goes right to that one, to the Dyooa's tomb tent. Bunelya said: "In the land of the deceased Dyooa, it will break the tomb tent of the dead Dyooa. And it will take out Dyooa, it will eat him, this polar bear." Well, this Dyooa, when he was dying, when he was leaving, he probably said so. Leave here my bows, here. Dyooa so, he got afraid, probably, he got afraid. So, well. He scattered his tomb tent in two directions. Dyooa jumped to his feet. Bunelya has been standing nearby for long: "Bunelya, where, where, say! Bunelya, where, where?" Bunelya said. He thinks to himself: That's what I did to you, probably. You were not dead, you were alive.
